newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover down 9 pct mo/mo in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover down 9 pct mo/mo in Sept.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) September turnover fell 9.17 percent to 160.597 million dinars ($31.87 million), the Belgrade bourse said on Tuesday.
The reduced turnover came despite a slight increase in the number of deals. September's total inched rose to 750 from 738 transactions worth 175.324 million dinars in August.
The BSE director Pava Zecevic blamed the turnover decline on a new central bank regulation introduced to tighten its grip on money supply and inflation.
"September turnover on the bourse eased on reduced market liquidity, which deteriorated after the central bank introduced a 10 percent reserve requirement," she told Reuters.
The central bank's measure forced many issuers to seek fresh borrowing, but demand for their securities remained weak, Zecevic said.
The investors' lack of enthusiasm for the increased supply of securities did not provoke severe fluctuations in interest rates, she added.
Traders said daily interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills moved up to 0.45 from 0.40 percent after the central bank announced the reserve requirement.
But according to Zecevic, the situation on the market started to improve and there was no longer reason for investors to be reluctant.
The commercial paper segment generated 46 percent and the central bank short-term bonds 45 percent of the total monthly turnover.

The central bank short-term bonds regained investor interest after the National Bank of Yugoslavia deliberately pushed the annual interest rate on those securities from 60.7 to 102.88 percent and then to 115.61 percent.
The bank also halved the bond's maturity to 30 days.
Treasury bills accounted for seven percent of the total September turnover while certificates of deposit made up another two percent of turnover.

September saw no deals in forward contracts selling agricultural produce. However, activity in this market segment could pick up from October 3, when a new tranche of wheat selling forward contracts begins to trade. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
